name: Minpentai Play, solo against the computer, v1

rules.text: The board is 15 x 10 squares.
The board has edges and corners.
A glider that would leave the board turns back on that side instead, and stays put for that step.

source.note: Starting in your own corner is from the book (c4-b94).

rules.text: Each side starts with 2 towers (Cyan at (1, 2) and (1, 7), Amber at (13, 2) and (13, 7)) and there are six rocks, all mirrored.

source.note: In the book they are "symbols"; the tower shape is invented.

rules.text: A tower is your score, your sight, and where you may place.
A glider moves one square a step in a straight line, up, down, left or right (diagonally too only under the "diag" rule), and never stops on its own.
A square blocks a glider: the first hit cracks it and turns the glider straight back; the second breaks the square and the glider. Any glider cracks any square, its own side's too.

source.note: Bouncing only is invented; in the book gliders hitting rocks can make more gliders.

rules.text: A rock is fixed, turns every glider straight back, and never breaks.
Every glider moves at the same moment.
Two gliders of different sides break each other if they head for the same square, swap squares, or cross. A side's own gliders pass through each other.

source.note: In the book a stray glider can wreck its own side (c4-b109); left out here.

rules.text: A glider reaching an opponent's tower destroys it and breaks. Your own tower turns it straight back.

source.note: The book's boards fill with debris (c4-b140).

rules.text: Broken pieces leave nothing behind.
A setup turn at step 0, then a turn to act every 12 steps; between turns the match runs on its own.
8 points a turn: glider 4, square 1, tower 4. Unspent points are lost.
Place on any empty square within 3 squares, counting diagonals, of a tower you had when the turn began.
Both sides place at the same time without seeing each other's choices; two pieces placed on one square cancel each other.
You see every square within 3 of one of your towers; the rest is dark.
Rocks are shown everywhere; an opponent's tower you cannot see is shown where you last saw it.
A side with no towers left loses; both at the same step is a draw.
At step 96 the match stops: most towers wins, equal is a draw.
You may resign; it counts as a loss.
One of four new rules is drawn from the seed at the start of every match, and both players see it.
The computer players see only what their towers light (Play's; Learn's practice bot is not part of this ruleset).
A match's seed is a whole number from 0 to 999,999. Its first random number draws the new rule; the computer player takes the rest, in order.
